answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Locking. Each agent’s identity is bound to a trajectory of behavioural features recorded at every epoch, and reputation at epoch N is only valid if its feature vector stays within a tolerance ball of the vector at epoch N-1. An attacker spinning up fresh sybils must carry each one across many epochs without drifting, so the cost is time plus sustained compute per identity, not a one-time payment. Any identity that jumps to a new vertex of behaviour space is quarantined at the jetty and denied forwarding rights. Honest agents that change gradually remain in the harbor,
